drafted_from: tool:google-account-find_my_mailbox's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Which Gmail address is my connection, and where does its mail stand now? Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-find_my_mailbox as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Which Gmail address is my connection, and where does its mail stand now?" and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-find_my_mailbox, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"}}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as GET  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/profile.
4. Keep the historyId it answers; hand it to tool:google-account-list_new_mail as since.

worked_examples.title: Find which mailbox a connection is on a sample input
worked_examples.ask: Which Gmail address is my connection, and where does its mail stand now?
worked_examples.given: read from tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (its invoke url, method and body_template) and checked against tools/read-and-write-gmail/test/rows.test.mjs. The connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery, which belongs to sam@example.com. The call it makes: GET the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/profile.
worked_examples.hands_back: Gmail answers {"emailAddress":"sam@example.com","historyId":"482913"}. Keep the historyId: it is the since value for tool:google-account-list_new_mail.
